- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price is falling.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 7–14 days; apply downward correction of 2–5% to avoid overreaction.  
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, consider mean reversion bias; reduce forecast toward historical mean by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is neutral or mixed, model often fails to capture short-term volatility; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if recent 5-day range is tight.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated “reversals” (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to match sentiment momentum.
